Feet very wide, shift your weight onto one leg while keeping the other straight out to the side. The cossack squat builds hip and ankle mobility in a deep position.
:::

::: step assisted-pistol
Hold a fixed support (a door frame, bar or post) and lower on one leg with the other straight in front. Use your hands as much as you need, then reduce the help session after session.
:::

::: step pistol
Unassisted: arms forward for balance, lower under control on one foot, then stand back up without bouncing. Go back to the assisted version if your heel lifts or your knee caves in.
:::

## How to train

| Block | Exercise | Volume |
|---|---|---|
| Warm-up | Ankle and hip mobility, squats | 5 minutes |
| Strength | Current step, each leg | 3 sets |
| Control | Slow single-leg box squats to a chair | 3 sets of 5 per leg |
| Mobility | Deep squat hold | 2 × 30 seconds |

**Box squats to a chair** are very effective: sit down slowly on one leg, then stand up with both. Lower the box over the weeks.

## Common mistakes

- **Heel lifting.** A sign of stiff ankles: work on mobility and keep using a support.
- **Knee caving in.** Keep your knee in line with your toes, even at the bottom.
- **Dropping into the bottom.** Control the descent: the way up starts from a stable bottom position.
- **Training one side only.** Always train both legs, starting with the weaker one.

## Frequently asked questions

### Why do I fall backwards in a pistol squat?

Usually because of limited ankle mobility or an upright torso. Reach your arms forward, lean your torso slightly and practise with a support or a small weight held in front of you.

### Are pistol squats bad for your knees?

Done progressively, with your knee in line and no pain, they’re an excellent exercise. If your knee hurts, go back to split squats and get professional advice.

### How long does it take to do a pistol squat?

With good mobility, a few weeks of regular practice is often enough. If your ankles limit you, it takes longer while you gain range.

All six steps animated, your sets logged per leg, and the camera coach to track your squat depth.
:::

articles.title: Beginner calisthenics program: a 3-day plan to get started
articles.description: A beginner calisthenics program with two workouts, A and B, alternated three times a week: exercises, sets, reps, rest times and how to progress.
articles.markdown:
Want to start calisthenics but not sure where to begin? This **beginner calisthenics program** fits into two workouts, A and B, alternated three times a week. It trains your whole body, needs very little equipment and gives you clear benchmarks to progress week after week.

It follows the same principles as the beginner programs in KALIST: few exercises, clean technique, and a target that only goes up when you’re ready.

## How the program works

- **Full body every session.** Push, pull, legs and core: as a beginner, training each area two to three times a week gives the best results.
- **Rep ranges.** Instead of a fixed number you aim for, say, 8 to 12 reps. When you hit the top of the range on every set, two sessions in a row, move to a harder variation.
- **A rest day between sessions.** Monday, Wednesday and Friday, for example.
- **Technique first.** A rep that loses its alignment doesn’t count.

## Equipment

The floor is enough for most exercises. A **pull-up bar** (doorway or park bar) is strongly recommended for pulling. A low bar, rings or straps let you do Australian rows. Two sturdy chairs can replace parallel bars for assisted dips.

## Warm-up (5 to 8 minutes)

Arm circles, wrist rotations, 10 slow squats, 10 easy incline push-ups and a 20-second hang from the bar. The goal is to reach your first set with warm joints, not tired muscles.

## Workout A

::: moves pushup, australian-row, squat
:::

| Exercise | Sets × reps | Rest |
|---|---|---|
| Push-ups (or incline push-ups) | 3 × 8 to 12 | 90 s |
| Australian rows | 3 × 8 to 12 | 90 s |
| Bodyweight squats | 3 × 12 to 15 | 60 s |
| Front plank | 3 × 20 to 30 s | 45 s |
| Hollow body | 2 × 15 to 20 s | 45 s |

## Workout B

::: moves negative-pullup, assisted-dip, lunge
:::

| Exercise | Sets × reps | Rest |
|---|---|---|
| Negative pull-ups (or active hangs) | 3 × 3 to 5 | 2 min |
| Assisted dips | 3 × 6 to 10 | 90 s |
| Reverse lunges | 3 × 8 to 10 per leg | 60 s |
| Glute bridges | 3 × 12 to 15 | 60 s |
| Side plank | 2 × 20 s per side | 45 s |

## Your week

| Week | Monday | Wednesday | Friday |
|---|---|---|---|
| Week 1 | A | B | A |
| Week 2 | B | A | B |

Follow this rhythm for **six weeks**, then take stock: which exercises have become easy? Move to the next variation (incline push-ups to full push-ups, negatives to pull-ups) and start a new cycle.

## Scaling each exercise

Every exercise has an easier and a harder version:

- **Push-ups**: wall → incline → knee → full → diamond.
- **Pulling**: Australian rows with bent knees → straight legs → negatives → pull-ups.
- **Legs**: squat → reverse lunge → split squat → Bulgarian split squat → pistol squat.
- **Core**: plank → hollow body → tuck L-sit.

You’ll find all of these, animated, in the [exercise library](/en/exercises/).

::: note
Sharp joint pain is not muscle soreness: stop the exercise and go back to an easier variation. If in doubt, ask a health professional.
:::

## Frequently asked questions

### How long before I see results from calisthenics?

Rep numbers often improve within two to three weeks as your body learns to coordinate the movements. Visible physical changes usually take several weeks of consistent training, along with good food and sleep.

### Can I do this program every day?

It’s not recommended: muscles and tendons get stronger during recovery. On rest days, walk, stretch or practise balance gently.

### I don’t have a pull-up bar. What should I do?

Replace pulling with Australian rows on rings or straps, or get a doorway pull-up bar: it’s the single most useful piece of calisthenics equipment. Without pulling, the program is unbalanced.

### When should I start training skills like the muscle-up?

Once your basics are solid: around 8 to 10 pull-ups and 10 dips for the muscle-up, for example. The [progression guides](/en/guides/) list the prerequisites for each skill.

::: cta A smarter version of this plan, in KALIST
Eight programs per level, targets that rise automatically after two successful sessions, and a camera coach that counts your reps.
:::

articles.title: Calisthenics at home with no equipment: 12 exercises to start
articles.description: 12 calisthenics exercises you can do at home with no equipment, for upper body, legs and core, plus a 20-minute beginner circuit.
articles.markdown:
No gym, no bar, no problem: calisthenics works very well **at home with no equipment**. A bit of floor, a wall and some consistency are enough to train your whole body and progress towards harder exercises.

Here are 12 bodyweight exercises grouped by area, followed by a 20-minute circuit that combines them. All of them are in the KALIST library with their animation and technique cues.

## Upper body: pushing

::: moves knee-pushup, pushup, pike-pushup
:::

1. **Knee push-ups**: the entry point. Keep a straight line from knees to shoulders.
2. **Push-ups**: body braced, elbows at roughly 30 to 60° from your torso, chest to the floor or close to it.
3. **Pike push-ups**: hips high, they shift the work to your shoulders and prepare you for the [handstand](/en/guides/handstand-progression/).

## Legs and glutes

::: moves squat, lunge, split-squat
:::

4. **Bodyweight squats**: heels down, knees tracking over your toes.
5. **Reverse lunges**: gentler on the knees than forward lunges.
6. **Split squats**: feet fixed, straight down and up, great for single-leg strength.

::: moves glute-bridge, calf-raise
:::

7. **Glute bridges**: lying on your back, lift your hips by squeezing your glutes.
8. **Calf raises**: on a step for more range, holding on for balance.

## Core

::: moves plank, side-plank, hollow, dead-bug
:::

9. **Front plank**: shoulders over elbows, lower back not sagging.
10. **Side plank**: hips high, body in line.
11. **Hollow body**: the base position of every skill, lower back pressed into the floor.
12. **Dead bug**: opposite arm and leg extend slowly, lower back stays down.

## The 20-minute circuit

Go through the exercises without stopping, then rest 2 minutes at the end of each round. Do 3 rounds.

| Exercise | Time or reps |
|---|---|
| Push-ups (or knee push-ups) | 8 to 12 |
| Squats | 15 |
| Pike push-ups | 6 to 8 |
| Reverse lunges | 8 per leg |
| Glute bridges | 12 |
| Front plank | 30 s |
| Hollow body | 20 s |

Three sessions a week, with a rest day between them, is enough to make clear progress within a few weeks.

## What about pulling?

That’s the real limit of training without equipment: it’s hard to train your back with nothing to pull on. The simplest fix is a **doorway pull-up bar**: cheap and quick to install. It unlocks hangs, [negative pull-ups](/en/guides/first-pull-up/) and eventually pull-ups.

Until then, strengthen your upper back with planks and hollow holds, and keep your shoulder blades active in your push-ups.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can you build muscle with calisthenics at home?

Yes, especially as a beginner, as long as you make the exercises progressively harder: a harder variation, a slower tempo or more reps. Sleep and nutrition do the rest.

### How long should a session last?

Twenty to forty minutes is enough. Consistency beats duration.

### Should I train every day?

No: three sessions a week is an excellent rhythm to start. On rest days, walking and gentle mobility help you recover.

::: cta Your home workouts, guided
KALIST gives you no-equipment programs, shows every movement as an animation and counts your reps with your phone camera.
:::

Want a full plan? Follow the [beginner calisthenics program](/en/blog/beginner-calisthenics-program/) with three sessions a week.

articles.title: Street workout vs calisthenics: what’s the difference?
articles.description: Street workout and calisthenics both mean bodyweight training. Their origins, differences, disciplines and how to get started with either.
articles.markdown:
**Street workout** or **calisthenics**? Both terms come up constantly in bodyweight training, sometimes as synonyms, sometimes as two different things. Here’s what they share, what sets them apart, and how to choose your way in.

## Calisthenics: training with your body weight

The word **calisthenics** comes from the Greek *kállos*, beauty, and *sthénos*, strength. It means training that uses your own body weight as resistance: push-ups, pull-ups, dips, squats and core work, then more advanced skills.

It’s a broad term. People do calisthenics at home, in the gym or at the park, for strength, fitness or skills.

## Street workout: calisthenics in the street

**Street workout** grew out of training in public spaces: park bars, outdoor fitness areas and urban structures. It took off in the 2000s through videos shared online, with a strong group and showcase culture.

Street workout has its own disciplines:

- **freestyle**: dynamic moves on the bar (spins, releases, combinations);
- **static holds**: skills such as the [front lever](/en/guides/front-lever-progression/), the [planche](/en/guides/planche-progression/) or the human flag;
- **strength and endurance**: rep challenges and sometimes weighted work.

Competitions exist in many countries, in both freestyle and strength.

## So what’s the difference?

| | Calisthenics | Street workout |
|---|---|---|
| Definition | Bodyweight training | Calisthenics practised outdoors, with its own culture |
| Where | Anywhere: home, gym, park | Mostly parks and urban structures |
| Goal | Strength, fitness, skills | Skills, freestyle, performance, community |
| Equipment | From nothing to bars, rings, parallettes | Park bars, parallel bars |

In practice, **street workout is one way of doing calisthenics**. The basic exercises are the same; the setting, the culture and some disciplines (like freestyle) differ.

## How to get started

Whatever you call it, the foundations are the same:

::: moves pushup, pullup, dip
:::

1. **Build the basics**: push-ups, pull-ups, dips, squats and core. The [beginner program](/en/blog/beginner-calisthenics-program/) organises them into three sessions a week.
2. **Pick a first skill**: your [first pull-up](/en/guides/first-pull-up/), the [L-sit](/en/guides/l-sit-progression/) or the [handstand](/en/guides/handstand-progression/) are all beginner-friendly.
3. **Go to the park** if you have one nearby: the atmosphere and advice from experienced athletes often save a lot of time.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is street workout suitable for beginners?

Yes. Street workout parks welcome every level, and low bars let you start with Australian rows or assisted dips.

### Do I need a gym for calisthenics?

No. Home is enough to start, and a park or a pull-up bar lets you go further. See [12 exercises to do at home with no equipment](/en/blog/calisthenics-at-home-no-equipment/).

### Calisthenics or weight training?

Both build strength. Calisthenics adds body control, balance and skills to learn; weight training lets you load each muscle precisely. Many people combine the two.

::: cta Calisthenics, from the park to your pocket
The KALIST Journey takes you from Beginner to Expert, with 94 animated movements and seven skill paths.
:::
